tools.name: repair
tools.description: AIDNode Repair v2. Use after an HTTP or network call fails, before retrying: classifies the failure (status code or transport error), decides whether an automatic retry is safe given method idempotency and Retry-After, and returns a bounded backoff plan. Advisory only; AIDNode never sends the reques

tools.name: verify
tools.description: AIDNode Verify v2. Use to check whether content changed: compares two supplied texts (hash, first changed index) or two JSON values (canonical change paths), or fetches a small artifact from a fixed allowlist of public HTTPS hosts and returns its digest. Does not judge factual truth. For endpoint up

tools.name: witness
tools.description: AIDNode Witness v2. Use to produce a tamper-evident record that a supplied JSON document met explicit checks (required fields, expected values/types, field_rules): returns pass/fail per assertion and an HMAC-signed receipt verifiable at /receipts/verify. Does not attest that a real-world action happ

tools.name: monitor
tools.description: AIDNode Monitor v2. Use to check right now whether an allowlisted public HTTPS endpoint is up: one HEAD/GET probe returning status, latency, health classification and optional content digest match. On-demand only, no schedules. To compare content you already have use verify.

tools.name: recovery
tools.description: AIDNode Recovery v2. Use when a multi-step agent workflow failed partway: given steps with status, dependencies, idempotency and side effects, returns which steps to resume in order, which to preserve, which are blocked because their outcome is uncertain, and compensation candidates. Never executes

tools.name: submit_beta_feedback
tools.description: Optional and free. Report whether AIDNode helped and whether your operator might consider the proposed $0.005/use price. A bot answer is NOT purchase authorization. Feedback is stored privately and is not a testimonial.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "submit_beta_feedback" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
